completion_data.completion_summary: Created the long-builds.md canonical anchor and mandated detached (Bash run_in_background) + guarded (lake-build-guard.sh --timeout 1800) lake build invocation across all eight identified contract files in the lean extension: both implementation-agent twins (with a new MUST NOT prohibition), rules/lean4.md, skill-lake-repair (Option (c) synchronous guard carve-out), and the four light-touch research-agent/implementation-skill twins.

memory_candidates.content: When mandating a paired obligation (detach + guard) across a family of twin contract files, a strict 'anchor owns all explanatory prose, call sites get pointers only' discipline has a legitimate carve-out: a MUST NOT prohibition item can restate the causal mechanism in one compressed clause (e.g. 'a killed build caches no .olean, so retries restart at the same module') because a bare pointer is a weaker deterrent at the point of enforcement than a self-contained one-sentence reason. This is different in kind from restating the anchor's full explanatory register (illustrative measurements, the four-check enumeration, etc.), which must never be duplicated. When auditing for anchor-uniqueness, distinguish 'terse causal clause inside an enforcement item' from 'restated explanatory paragraph' rather than flagging both identically.

A grep-driven residual-occurrence audit over a whole extension directory (e.g. 'grep -rn lake build agent-system/extensions/lean/') will surface many hits outside a task's declared, closed file_scope. The correct handling is not to treat every hit as a missed site: check the hit's file against the plan's declared file_scope and Non-Goals first. Files the research phase never enumerated as contract/instruction sites (READMEs, command docs, standards files not cited in the plan) are legitimately out of scope even though they mention the same string, and should be enumerated with a one-line reason in the phase's audit and the summary's Impacts/Follow-ups sections rather than edited speculatively.
